does: Brings hot food down to the cold of the fridge quickly, so that it keeps well and so that a cold dish is truly cold.

intro.what: Food is cooled in shallow containers, with an iced-water bath assisting the temperature change.
intro.why: Container shape affects how heat leaves the food. Cold dishes also need tasting at their serving temperature.

how: Move the hot food out of its pot into a wide, shallow container.
Stand the container in iced water and stir now and then.
Put it in the fridge, uncovered, once it has stopped steaming.
Cover it when it is cold. Taste a cold dish again before serving, because cold dulls salt.

cues.text: The container is cold to the hand all over, with no warm core.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving a large pot of stock to cool by itself on the stove, where its middle stays warm for a long time.
mistakes.fix: Divide it into shallow containers and cool them in iced water.

mistakes.mistake: Seasoning a soup while it is hot and serving it cold.
mistakes.fix: Taste it again when it is cold.

quiz.question: Why move food into shallow containers?
choices: Heat can leave more readily than from a deep pot.
The shallow shape helps a surface skin trap heat inside.
A shallow layer holds its centre warm for longer.
quiz.because: Shallower containers reduce the depth of food that heat must travel through.

quiz.question: How does the iced-water bath assist this method?
choices: It is poured into the food to dilute it.
It draws heat from the container while the food is stirred.
It warms the container before refrigeration.
quiz.because: Cold water around the container helps remove heat; stirring distributes temperature within the food.

quiz.question: What handling cue is described for the chilled container?
choices: The rim feels cold while the base stays warm.
Steam continues rising from the centre.
It feels cold across its surface.
quiz.because: An evenly cold container is the handling observation described here; it does not measure the food’s centre temperature.

quiz.question: A cold soup tastes underseasoned after being seasoned hot. What should you do?
choices: Taste it again at its serving temperature.
Assume the hot tasting still describes it exactly.
Warm it solely to avoid tasting it cold.
quiz.because: Cold changes flavour perception, so seasoning should be assessed again for the cold dish.
